complete, perfect.. 1Th.5:23.†
SYN.: ὁλόκληρος (which see), τέλειος. "As regards meaning, ὁλόκληρος can hardly be distinguished from ὁλοτελής though, in accordance with its derivation, it draws more special attention to the several parts to which the wholeness spoken of extends, no part being wanting or lacking in completeness" (M, Th., 78) (AS)

G3648.d:
ὁλό-κληρος, -ον
(ὅλος, κλῆρος, i.e. with all that has fallen by lot), [in LXX: Lev.23:15, Eze.15:5 (תָּמִים), Deu.27:6, Jos.8:31 (9:2) (שָׁלֵם), Zec.11:16 (נָצַב ni.), Wis.15:3, 1Ma.4:47, 4Ma.15:17 * ;] 
complete, entire; in NT in ethical sense (as Wis, 4Mac, ll. with), 1Th.5:23; ὁ. καὶ τέλειοι, Jas.1:4.†
SYN.: ὁλοτελής (which see), τελειος (Tr., Syn., § xxii) (AS)

G6034.d:
ἐν-ορκίζω, 
[in LXX: Neh.13:25 A (שָׁבַע hi.)* ;] 
to adjure: with dupl. accusative (like ορκίζω, which see), ὑμᾶς τ. κῦριον, 1Th.5:27.†
(AS)

G5232.d:
ὑπερ-αυξάνω 
to increase beyond measure: 2Th.1:3 (see Lft., Notes, 98).†
(AS)

G7013.d:
ἐν-καυκάομαι 
(Rec. ἐγκ-, see: ἐν), -ῶμαι [in LXX: 51(52):1 96(97):7 (הָלַל hithp.); Ps 73(74):4 (שָׁאַג); Ps 105(106):47 (שָׁבַח)* ;] 
to take pride in, glory in: before ἐν, 2Th.1:4.†
(AS)

G1730.d:
ἔν-δειγμα, -τος
(ἐνδείκνυμι), 
a plain token, proof: 2Th.1:5 (cf. ἔνδειξις, which refers rather to the "act of proving"; ἔ., with the passive formation, to the thing proved, see Lft., Notes, 100; M, Th., l.with).†
SYN.: τεκμήριον (AS)

G5099.d:
τίνω 
[in LXX: Pro.27:12 (τ. ζημίαν, for עָנַשׁ ni.), etc. ;] 
to pay: t. δίκην (cf. Pr, l.with), to pay penalty, 2Th.1:9 (see M, Th., in l).†
(AS)

G1740.d:
ἐν-δοξάζω 
[in LXX for כָּבַד ni., Exo.14:4, 17-18, Eze.28:22, etc.; for עָרַץ, Psa.89:7; Sir.38:6, al. ;] 
to glorify: pass., 2Th.1:10-12.†
(AS)

G1997.d:
ἐπι-συν-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἐπισυνάγω), [in LXX: 2Ma.2:7 * ;] 
a gathering together, assembly: Heb.10:25; before ἐπί, 2Th.2:1 (cf. 2Mac, l.with).†
(AS)

G2015.d:
ἐπιφάνεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἐπιφανής), [in LXX: 2Ki.7:23 (יָרֵא), Est.5:1, Amo.5:22, 2Ma.2:21 2Mac 3:24 2Mac 5:4 2Mac 12:22 2Mac 14:16 2Mac 15:27, 3Ma.2:9 3Mac 5:8 3Mac 5:51,* ;] (in late Gk. and Inscr., frequently of deities, see MM, Exp., xiv) 
a manifestation, appear­ance: 2Th.2:8, 1Ti.6:14, 2Ti.1:10 4:1 4:8, Tit.2:13 (cf. M, Th., 148 f.).†
(AS)

G3401.d:
μιμέομαι, -οῦμαι
(μῖμος, a mimic, an actor), [in LXX: Psa.31:6, Wis.4:2 15:9, 4Ma.9:23 4Mac 9:13 : * ;] 
to imitate: 2Th.3:7 3:9 Heb.13:7, 3Jn.11.†
(AS)

G0812.d:
ἀτακτέω -ῶ
(ἄτακτος), 
primarily, of soldiers marching, to be out of order, to quit the ranks; hence, metaphorically, to be remiss, fail in the performance of duty (in π., of truancy on the part of an apprentice): 2Th.3:7 (on ἀ. and its cognates, see M, Th., 152 ff.; MM, s.vv.).†
(AS)

G4020.d:
περι-εργάζομαι 
[in LXX: Wis.8:5 א1, Sir.3:23 * ;] 
1. to waste one's labour about a thing. 
2. to be a busybody: 2Th.3:11 (cf. Plat., Apol., 19 B).†
(AS)

G2569.d:
καλο-ποιέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Lev.5:4 F (καλῶς π., B) * ;] 
to do well, act honourably: 2Th.3:13 (cf. Gal.6:9 τὸ καλὸν π.).†
(AS)

G4593.d:
σημειόω, -ῶ
(σημεῖον), [in LXX: Psa.4:6 (נָשָׂא)* ;] 
to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: 2Th.3:14 (frequently in π.; see ICC, M, Th., in l).†
(AS)

G2085.d:
ἑτεροδιδασκαλέω, -ῶ 
to teach other or different doctrine: 1Ti.1:3 6:3 (cf. CGT, in l; Milligan, NTD, 102).†
(AS)

G3454.d:
μῦθος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Wis.17:4 A, Sir.20:19 * ;] 
1. speech, con­versation. 
2. (a) a story, narrative (Hom.); 
(b) later, opposite to λόγος (a true narrative) = Lat. fabula, a myth, fable, fiction: 1Ti.1:4 4:7, 2Ti.4:4, Tit.1:14, 2Pe.1:16.†
SYN.. λόγος, q.v (AS)

G1076.d:
γενεαλογία, -ας, ἡ (see previous word); 
1. the making of a pedigree. 
2. a genealogy: pl., 1Ti.1:4, Tit.3:9 (see CGT, in l., and ib. Intr., xlix ff.; DB, ii, p. 141).
† (AS)

G0562.d:
ἀπέραντος, -ον
(περαίνω, to complete, finish) [in LXX: Job.36:26 (חֵקֶר אַיִן) 3Mac.20 * ;] 
endless, interminable: 1Ti.1:4.†
(AS)

G6027.d:
ἐκ-ζήτησις, -εως, ἡ 
(ἐκζητέω), 
a questioning (RV), subject for dispute: 1Ti.1:4.†
(AS)

G0795.d:
ἀστοχέω, -ῶ
(στόχος, a mark), [in LXX: Sir.7:19 8:9 * ;] 
to miss the mark, fail: with genitive, 1Ti.1:6 (so in π., MM, see word); before περί, 1Ti.6:21, 2Ti.2:18.†
(AS)

G1624.d:
ἐκ-τρέπω 
[in LXX for הָפַךְ, Amo.5:8 * ;] 
to turn out of the course, turn aside, with accusative Pass., with middle sense, intrans., to turn aside: Heb.12:13 (R, txt., for be put out of joint, R, mg., see Thayer, see word Westc., in l); figuratively, before εἰς, 1Ti.1:6; ἐπί, 2Ti.4:4; ὀπίσω, 1Ti.5:15; with accusative, to shun, avoid: 1Ti.6:20.†
(AS)

G3150.d:
ματαιολογία, -ας, ἡ
(ματαιολόγος), 
idle or foolish talk: 1Ti.1:6.†
(AS)

G1226.d:
δια-βεβαιόομαι, -οῦμαι 
to affirm confidently: Tit.3:8; before περί, 1Ti.1:7 (Cremer, 140).†
(AS)

G3545.d:
νομίμως 
adv. (νόμιμος, conformable to law), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:18 * ;] 
rightly, lawfully: 1Ti.1:8, 2Ti.2:5.†
(AS)

G0506.d:
ἀνυπότακτος, -ον
(ά- neg., ὑποτάσσω) [in Sm.: 1Ki.2:12 10:27 (for LXX, λοιμός, בֵּן בְּלִיַּעַל)* ;] 
of things, not subject to rule: Heb.2:8; of persons, unruly: 1Ti.1:9, Tit.1:6, 10 (MM, VGT, see word).†
(AS)

G0462.d:
ἀν-όσιος, -ον
(ἀ- neg., ὅσιος), [in LXX: Eze.22:9 (זִמָּה, Wis.12:4, 2Ma.7:34 2Mac 8:32, 3Ma.2:2 3Mac 5:7, 4Ma.12:11 * ;] 
unholy, profane (Cremer, 464): 1Ti.1:9, 2Ti.3:2 (MM, VGT, see word).†
(AS)

G0952.d:
βέβηλος, -ον 
(βαίνω, whence βηλός, a threshold), [in LXX chiefly for חֹל ;] 
1. permitted to be trodden, accessible (see DCG, ii, 422b); hence, 
2. (opposite to ἱερός) unhallowed, profane: of things, 1Ti.4:7 6:20, 2Ti.2:16; of men, 1Ti.1:9, Heb.12:16 (cf. κοινός; Cremer, 140).
† (AS)

G3964.d:
πατρολῴας (-αλῴας, Rec.; in cl. -αλοίας, see Bl., § 3, 3; 6, 2, and cf. μητρολῴας), -ου, ὁ 
(πατήρ + ἀλοιάω, to smite), 
(a) a parricide: 1Ti.1:9 (Av, R, txt.); 
(b) a smiter of his father : ib. (R, mg.).†
(AS)

G3389.d:
μητρολῴας (Rec. -αλῴας, in cl., -αλοίας, see B1., § 3, 3; 6, 2), -ου, ὁ 
(μήτρρ + ἀλοιάω, to smite) 
(a) a matricide: 1Ti.1:9 (AV, R, txt., but see infr.); 
(b) a smiter of his mother: 1Ti.1:9 (R, mg., cf. Exo.21:15, and see Ellic., CGT, in l).†
(AS)

G0409.d:
ἀνδρο-φόνος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: 2Ma.9:28 * ;] 
a man-slayer: 1Ti.1:9 (cf. φονεύς, and see MM, VGT, see word).†
(AS)

G0405.d:
ἀνδραποδιστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(ἀνδράποδον, a slave, captured in war) 
a slave-dealer, kidnapper: 1Ti.1:10 (see MM, VGT, see word).†
(AS)

G1965.d:
ἐπί-ορκος, -ον 
[in LXX: Zec.5:3 (שָׁבַע ni.) * ;] 
1. of oaths, sworn falsely. 
2. Of persons, perjured; as subst., a perjurer, false swearer: 1Ti.1:10.†
(AS)

G4386.d:
before; (adv.) before, formerly, an earlier time 
former, prior, Eph. 4:22; before, former, prior, Eph. 4:22; before, formerly, Jn. 6:62

G5250.d:
ὑπερ-πλεονάζω 
to abound exceedingly: 1Ti.1:14 (Ps Sol 5:19; Herm., Mand., v, 2, 5).†
(AS)

G0594.d:
ἀπο-δοχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἀποδέχομαι), 
acceptance, approbation (Field, Notes, 203): 1Ti.1:15 4:9 (Cremer, 686; MM, see word).†
(AS)

G5296.d:
ὑπο-τύπωσις, -εως, ἡ
(ὑποτυπόω, to delineate), 
an outline, sketch. Metaphorical, a pattern, example: 1Ti.1:16, 2Ti.1:13.†
SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, τύπος, ὑπόδειγμα (see DB, iii, 696b) (AS)

G0223J.d:
Ἀλέξανδρος, -ου, ὁ, 
Alexander 
1. Son of Simon of Cyrene: Mrk.15:21 
2. A kinsman of the High Priest: Act.4:6. 
3. A certain Jew: Act.19:33. 
4. A coppersmith: 1Ti.1:20. 
5. Perh. = 4 (see Ellic. on I Ti, l.with): 2Ti.4:14.
† (AS)

G1783.d:
ἐν-τευξις, -εως, ἡ
(ἐντυγχάνω, which see), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:3 * ;] 
1. a lighting upon, meeting with. 
2. conversation. 
3. a petition (in this sense common in π.; cf. Deiss., BS, 121 f., 146; MM, Exp., iii): 1Ti.4:5; p1., 1Ti.2:1.†
SYN.: δέησις (which see) (AS)

G2263.d:
ἤρεμος-ον 
[in LXX Est.3:13 A* ;] 
quiet, tranquil (Luc., al.): 1Ti.2:2.†
SYN: ἡσύχιος, q.v 
(AS)

G2272.d:
ἡσύχιος, -α, -ον
(= the more frequently ἥσυχος; cf. Wis.18:14, Sir.25:20), [in LXX: Isa.66:2 (רוּחַ נָכֶה)* ;] 
quiet, tranquil: 1Ti.2:2, 1Pe.3:4.†
SYN.: ἤρεμος, of tranquillity arising from without; ἡ., from within (see Ellic. on 1Ti, l.with; but also see CGT, ib.).† (AS)

G1236.d:
δι-άγω 
[in LXX for עבר hi., etc. ;] 
1. to carry over. 
2. Of time, to pass: βίον, 1Ti.2:2; absol., to live, before ἐν, Tit.3:3.†
(AS)

G4587.d:
σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ
(σεμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:12 * ;] 
gravity: 1Ti.2:2 3:4 (Vg. eastitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, see word), Tit.2:7.† 
(AS)

G0487.d:
ἀντί-λυτρον, -ου, τό 
[in Al.: Psa.49:9 * ;] 
a ransom: 1Ti.2:6 (see CGT, in l; and cf. λύτρον).†
(AS)

G2783.d:
κῆρυξ
(κήρ-, T), -υκος, ὁ [in LXX: Dan LXX TH Dan.3:4 (כָּרוֹז), Gen.41:43, Sir.20:15, 4Ma.6:4 * ;] 
a herald: 1Ti.2:7, 2Ti.1:11, 2Pe.2:5.†
(AS)

G2689.d:
κατα-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(καταστέλλω), [in LXX: Isa.61:3 (מַעֲטֶה)* ;] 
1. a letting down, checking. 
2. steadiness, quietness in demeanour. 
3. LXX and NT (cf. Plut., ii, 65 D; -ίζω = vestire), a garment, dress, attire: 1Ti.2:9 (but see Ellic., in l).†
(AS)

G2887.d:
κόσμιος, -ον (in cl. -α, -ον), 
(κόσμος), [in LXX: Ecc.12:9 (תָּקַן)* ;] 
orderly, decent, modest: 1Ti.2:9 (WH, mg., -ίως, which see) 1Ti.3:2.†
(AS)

G0127.d:
αἰδώς (-όος), -οῦς, ἡ, 
[in LXX: 3Ma.1:19 4:5 * ;] 
a sense of shame, modesty: 1Ti.2:9 (for exx., see MM, VGT, see word).†
SYN.: αἰσχύνη (see Thayer, 14; Tr., Syn., §xix; Cremer, 611 f.; CGT on I Ti, l.with). (AS)

G4117.d:
πλέγμα, -τος, τό
(πλέκω), [in Aq., Th.: Isa.28:5 * ;] 
what is woven or twisted (as basket-work, nets, etc.); a braiding (sc. τριχῶν, cf. 1Pe.3:3) : pl., 1Ti.2:9.†
(AS)

G2317.d:
θεοσέβεια, -ας, ἡ
(θεοσεβής), [in LXX Gen.20:11 (אֱלֹהִים יִרְאָה), Job.28:28 (אֲדֹנָי id.), Sir.1:24, Bar.5:4, 4Ma.7:6 4Mac 7:22, א 4Ma.15:28 א 4Ma.17:15 * ;] 
fear of God, godliness: 1Ti.2:10.†
(AS)

G0831.d:
αὐθεντέω, -ῶ
(αὐθέντης, i.e. αὐτο- ἕντης, one who acts on his own authority, in π., an autocrat; cf. Wis.12:6; cf. -ία, 3Ma.2:29; -ικος is frequently in vernacular, MM, see word) 
to govern, exercise authority over: 1Ti.2:12.†
(AS)

G3713.d:

(ἀ- ἐπιλαμβάνω) 
without reproach: 1Ti.3:2 5:7 6:14.†
SYN.: ἀμεμπτος, ἀνέγκλητος. It is stronger than these, for it implies not only that the man is of good report, but that he is deservedly so (cf. MM, VGT, see word). (AS)

G3524.d:
νηφάλιος (-λεος, Rec., in 1Ti, ll. with), -ον (in cl., -α, -ον), 
(νήφω), 
1. in cl., of drink, not mixed with wine. 
2. In later writers (Plut., al.), of persons, sober, temperate: 1Ti.3:2 3:11, Tit.2:2.†
(AS)

G4998.d:
σώφρων, -ον 
[in LXX: 4Ma.9:1-32 * ;] 
(a) of sound mind, sane, sensible; 
(b) self-controlled, sober-minded: 1Ti.3:2, Tit.1:8 2:2, 5 (Arist.).†
(AS)

G1317.d:
διδακτικός, -ή, -όν
(= cl. διδασκαλικός) 
apt at teaching: 1Ti.3:2, 2Ti.2:24.†
(AS)

G3943.d:
πάρ-οινος, -ον 
= cl., παροινικός (παρά, οἶνος), 
given to wine, drunken: 1Ti.3:3, Tit.1:7.†
(AS)

G4131.d:
πλήκτης, -ου, ὁ
(πλήσσω), [in Sm.: Psa.35:15 * ;] 
a striker, brawler: 1Ti.3:3, Tit.1:7 (Arist., Plut., al.).†
(AS)

G0146.d:
αἰσχροκερδής, -ες 
(αἰσχρός, κέρδος), 
greedy of base gains: 1Ti.3:3,8 Abbot-Smith omits 1Ti.3:3, Tit.1:7.†
(AS)

G0269.d:
ἄμαχος, -ον
(μάχη); 
1. invincible (frequently in cl.). 
2. abstaining from fighting, non-combatant (Xen.). Metaphorical (cf. MM, VGT, see word), not contentious: 1Ti.3:3, Tit.3:2.†
(AS)

G0866.d:
ἀ-φιλ-άργυρος, -ον 
without love of money, not avaricious; 1Ti.3:3, Heb.13:5. (For other instances, see MM, see word)†
(AS)

G3504.d:
νεό-φυτος, -ον
(νέος, φύω) [in LXX: Job.14:9, Psa.144:12, Isa.5:7 (נֶטַע), Psa.128:3 (שְׁתִל)* ;] 
newly planted (LXX). Metaphorical, as subst., ὁ ν., a new convert, neophyte, novice: 1Ti.3:6†
(AS)

G5187.d:
τυφόω, -ῶ
(τῦφος, smoke; metaphorically, conceit), 
prop., to wrap in smoke; used only metaphorically, to puff up, becloud with pride: pass., 1Ti.3:6 6:4, 2Ti.3:4 (Dem., Arist., al.).†
(AS)

G1351.d:
διλογος, -ον
(δίς, λέγω), 
1. in sense of διλογεῖν, -ία (Xen.), given to repetition. 
2. In NT, prob. (cf. δίγλωσσος, Pro.11:13, Sir.5:9) double-tongued: 1Ti.3:8.†
(AS)

βαθμός, -οῦ, ὁ, Ion. form of βασμός

a step (4Ki, l.with, of degrees of a dial); metaphorically, a degree, standing: 1Ti.3:13.† 
(AS)

G1019.d:
βραδύνω 
(βραδύς), [in LXX: Gen.43:10 (מההּ hith.), Deu.7:10, Isa.46:13 (אחר pi.), Si 32 (35):18 * ;] 
1. trans., to retard (Soph., Is, l.with). 
2. More frequently intrans., to be slow, to tarry: 1Ti.3:15, 2Pe.3:9.
† (AS)

G1477.d:
ἑδραίωμα, -τος, τό 
(ἑδραῖος), 
a support, bulwark, stay (Vg. fermamentum): 1Ti.3:15 (eccl.).†
(AS)

G3672.d:
ὁμολογουμένως 
adv. (ὁμ oλογέω), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:31 4Mac 7:16 4Mac 16:1 * ;] 
1. as agreed, conformably with. 
2. confessedly, by common consent: 1Ti.3:16.†
(AS)

G4490.d:
ῥητῶς 
adv. (ῥητός, stated, specified), 
in stated terms, expressly: 1Ti.4:1.†
(AS)

G5573.d:
ψευδο-λόγος, -ον
(ψευδής, λέγω), 
speaking falsely, lying: 1Ti.4:2 (Aristoph., Polyb., al.).†
(AS)

G2743.d:
καυστηριάζω (Rec. καυτηρ-, and so usually in Gk. writers, see Soph., Lex., see word) 
to mark by branding, brand (AV, scar, but see CGT, in l): metaphorically, pass. pf. ptcp., 1Ti.4:2 (cf. καυτήριον, 4Ma.15:22 *).†
(AS)

G3336.d:
μετά-λημψις (Rec. -ληψις), -εως, ἡ 
(μεταλαμβάνω) 
participation, taking, receiving: of food, 1Ti.4:3.†
(AS)

G2938.d:
κτίσμα, -τος, τό
(κτίζω), [in LXX: Wis.9:2 13:5 14:11, Sir.36:20 (17), Sir.38:34, 3Ma.5:11 * ;] 
1. (cl.) a colony. 
2. a created thing, creature: 1Ti.4:4, Jas.1:18, Rev.5:13 8:9.†
(AS)

G0579.d:
ἀπό-βλητος, -ον
(ἀποβάλλω), [in Aq.: Lev.7:18, al.; Sm.: Hos.9:3 (טָמֵא) ;] 
to be thrown away, rejected: 1Ti.4:4 (Hom., Plut.).†
(AS)

G1789.d:
ἐν-τρέφω 
to train up, nurture; pass., metaphorically, τοῖς λόγοις τ. πίστεως, 1Ti.4:6.†
(AS)

G1126.d:
γραώδης, -ες (γραῦς, an old woman, εἶδος), 
anile, old-womanish: 1Ti.4:7.†
(AS)

G1128.d:
γυμνάζω 
(γυμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.10:15 * ;] 
1. properly, to exercise naked. 
2. Generally, to exercise, train the body or mind: 1Ti.4:7, Heb.5:14 12:11, 2Pe.2:14.
† (AS)

G5624.d:
ὠφέλιμος, -ον
(ὠφελέω), 
useful, serviceable, profitable: with dative commod., Tit.3:8; before πρός, with accusative, 1Ti.4:8, 2Ti.3:16.†
(AS)

G0047.d:
ἁγνεία (WH, ἁγνία), 
[in LXX for טָהֳרָה, נָזִיר, נֶזֶר, etc. ;] 
purity: 1Ti.4:12, 5:2 (Cremer, 58. For exx. of ceremonial use in π., see MM, Exp., iv).†
(AS)

G1969.d:
ἐπι-πλήσσω 
1. to strike at, to punish.

G0001G.d:
Α, α, ἄλφα (which see), τό, indecl., 
alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet. As a numeral, ά = 1, α = 1000. As a prefix, it appears to have at least two and perhaps three distinct senses:
